questions.title: What is the purpose of the reference policy \(\pi_{\text{ref}}\) in Direct Preference Optimization?
questions.question_body:
The DPO formulation uses a “reference policy” \(\pi_{\text{ref}}(y|x)\), which I understand is usually first fine-tuned on high‑quality data (SFT). In practice, why do we need this separate reference distribution when training \(\pi_{\theta}\)? What would happen if we omitted it or set \(\pi_{\text{ref}}
     = \pi_{\theta}\)? How does it relate to the KL‑divergence term that appears in Eq.…?

questions.title: How does DPO eliminate explicit reward modeling while still respecting a KL‑constrained RL objective?
questions.question_body:
"DPO is a RL‑free algorithm that still optimizes for reward maximization under a KL constraint.…" Specifically, could you walk through the derivation from Eq.… (the constrained RL objective) to Eq.… (the re‑parameterised loss where \(r(x,y)= eta \, \log  rac{\pi_{	heta}(y|x)}{\pi_{	ext{ref}}(y|x)} +  eta \, \log Z(x)\)), explaining how solving for \(p^*
     = p(y_1 \succ y_2 | x)
     = \sigma(r^*(x,y_1)-r^*(x,y_2))
     \) leads directly to a cross‑entropy objective over policies.

questions.question_body:

questions.question_body:
"The gradient in Eq.‣6 includes σ(ĥr(x,y_l)-ĥr(x,y_w)) which weights updates by how much higher

$𝛑̂$ assigns probability to incorrect examples.…" Could you explain why this weighting prevents over‑confident updates and scales with κ (β)? What would happen if σ was replaced by 1?

questions.title: "Equivalence classes of reward functions" – why do different rewards trigger identical preferences?
questions.question_body:
"Lemma 1 states that if two rewards differ only by a function of x,
a(r−r')=f(x), then they induce identical preferences…"
How does this under‑specification arise from Plackett–Luce/Bradley–Terry assumptions, and why doesn’t it affect which optimal policy we recover?

questions.title:
"Theorem 1" – how do we know every acceptable reward can be rewritten as
$r(x,y)=β\,	frac{π(y|x)}{π_{	ext{ref}}(y|x)}$?
questions.question_body:
"The proof sketched in Appendix D shows that for any reward r there exists some π_r built via Eq.‣ leading to r = β [log π_r/π_{ref} + logZ]…"
Could you detail what makes this mapping bijective over equivalence classes and show explicitly how one reconstructs π_r from an arbitrary r?

questions.title: "Initialising π_ref when no SFT model exists" – practical guidelines
questions.question_body:
"When π^SFT is unavailable we initialise π_ref by maximising likelihood over preferred completions…"
How exactly should this be done computationally—e.g., is it just standard supervised finetuning on pairs (x,y_w), or do we need any special tricks? What are potential pitfalls here?

questions.title: "Scaling limits of DPO" – will it work for trillion‑parameter LMs?
questions.question_body:
"The discussion mentions future work scaling beyond 6B parameters."
From a computational point of view—no sampling loop implies fewer GPU passes—yet retrieving probabilities for whole sequences remains expensive.
What practical challenges might arise at extreme scale (e.g., flash-root memory constraints, computing log‑probabilities for long outputs), and do you foresee any theoretical barriers?
